newsitem.title: JAPAN: SWIMMING-U.S. RELAY TEAM OUTSHINES THOMPSON, RILEY.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-U.S. RELAY TEAM OUTSHINES THOMPSON, RILEY.

text.p: The U.S. men's medley relay team outshone American Jenny Thompson and Samantha Riley of Australia on the last day of the Pan Pacific swimming championships on Wednesday.
The team of Lenny Krayzelburg, Kurt Grote, Nathaniel Dusing and Neil Walker equalled the second-fastest time ever of three minutes 36.93 seconds in easily winning the men's 4x100 medley relay.
The time was equal to the U.S. gold-medal winning times at the Seoul and Barcelona Olympics.
The world record of 3:34.84 was set by the U.S. team at the Atlanta Olympics.
Thompson picked up her fifth gold medal and Riley blasted away from the field in the women's 200 metres breaststroke in the fourth-fastest time ever.
The United States won six of the 10 finals on offer to finish the four-day event with 19. Australia were second with 10.

Thompson anchored the U.S. team to victory in the women's 4x100 medley relay but said she was a little disappointed not to have won six golds after Olympic champion Le Jingyi of China edged her in the women's 50 freestyle.
"I wanted to win six golds, but I couldn't quite do it," said Thompson, who has won five Olympic gold medals.
"I was a stroke too short. I kind of glided into the wall and that cost me the race."
Riley's impressive win in 2:25.34 seconds nudged her a little closer to compatriot Rebecca Brown's 1994 world record of 2:24.76.
"I was a little disappointed about not breaking the world record, but I think it's just a matter of time," Riley said.
Japan's Masami Tanaka was second while Riley's South African rival and double Olympic champion Penny Heyns faded to sixth.
Riley earlier beat Heyns in the 100 breaststroke.
American Kristine Quance's time of 2:13.79 gave her a gold in the 200 individual medley to add to her earlier 400 individual medley title. Canadian Marianne Limpert was second.
Grote won the men's 200 breaststroke final in 2:14.05, beating Japan's Yoshiaki Okita and fellow American Tom Wilkens.
In the women's 800 freestyle, Olympic champion Brooke Bennett pulled steadily away to win in 8:26.36.
"I wanted to take it out hard, get comfortable and take the lead," the American said.
Costa Rica's Claudia Poll, who won the 200 and 400 freestyle races, finished second in 8:29.05.
Australia's Matthew Dunn edged out Canada's Curtis Myden and American Ron Karnaugh to take the men's 200 individual medley. Karnaugh, 31, was the oldest swimmer in Fukuoka.

The men's 50 freestyle gold was shared between Puerto Rico's Ricardo Busquests and American William Pilczuk after they finished in 22.42, and Australia's 17-year-old Grant Hackett overcame a fever to win the men's 1,500 freestyle in 15:13.25.
World-record holder Le gave China their sole gold with her 50 freestyle win over Thompson, who earlier edged Le out in the 100 freestyle.
China won only four medals in Fukuoka, three by Le who also had two silvers. She holds world records in both the 50 and 100 freestyle.

"I was not satisfied with my performance," Le said, adding she was in training for the Chinese national championships in October, from which China will select their team for the world championships in Perth in January.
China brought only five swimmers, compared with 52 for the United States and 34 for Australia.
About 300 swimmers from 22 countries and regions competed in the Pan Pacific championships, which are held every two years with the next meet in Sydney.
